The Hallam index of every square is thre.why: A made-up property ('Hallam index') given to a real class (squares). One Dolma hit (an unrelated use of the place name) and no mathematical use on the web.

sources.note: No mathematical index of that name; hits were Hallam Square in Sheffield and Hallam Street in London.

The perimeter of a square is four times.why: The perimeter formula P = 4ℓ, in the Square article as a formula and in school references as a sentence.

sources.quote: The Perimeter is 4 times the side length
sources.note: Followed by the formula Perimeter = 4a. The Wikipedia Square article gives it only as a formula (P=4ℓ).

Every face of a cube is a square..why: The cube is the solid with six square faces, stated in its article.

sources.quote: It has eight vertices and twelve straight edges of the same length, so that these edges form six square faces of the same size.
